solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Building housing unit, except for shelves

parts.note: bar means except, as in 'all bar one'
racks are frames of shelves

explanation.surface: A building houses a unit, apart from its shelving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Building housing unit' reads like a description of the next part of the clue, but it is the whole definition: a military unit lives there.
explanation.definitionFit: Barracks are the quarters where a military unit of soldiers is lodged.

clue.text: Girl threatened with beheading, a consequence of nits

parts.note: taken as written
nits are the eggs of lice, so lice follow from them

explanation.surface: A girl's head is threatened because she has nits.
explanation.walkthrough: The Queen of Hearts in Alice in Wonderland keeps shouting 'Off with her head!' at the heroine.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewis Carroll's heroine is threatened with execution by the Queen of Hearts in Wonderland.

clue.text: Desert island included in some catalogue, I think logically

parts.note: to rat is to desert one's side
I is the abbreviation for island
something included in a catalogue is on a list

explanation.surface: A cataloguer reasons that a desert island belongs in some listing.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the kind of thing the answer would say of themself: a self-description rather than a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A rationalist bases belief on reason, so would describe their own thinking as logical.

clue.text: Rogue donkey that hurts large fowl

parts.note: a cur is a contemptible scoundrel
an ass is a donkey
ow is what you say when something hurts

explanation.surface: A wild donkey injures a big bird.
explanation.walkthrough: A curassow is a large turkey-like bird of Central and South American forests.
explanation.definitionFit: The curassow is a big ground-dwelling game bird related to guans, so a large fowl.

clue.text: Royal house one leaves puzzling at a corgi's huge box

indicators.note: something puzzling is confused, so the letters are jumbled into a new order
one is the letter I, and leaving means it departs from the letters that follow

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A royal household is baffled by an enormous box for a corgi.
explanation.walkthrough: Corgis are the late Queen's famous dogs, which keeps the royal picture going. Removing I leaves fifteen letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Saxe-Coburg-Gotha was the name of the British royal dynasty before it was changed to Windsor in 1917.

clue.text: Fashionable son frequently changed underwear

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son
a nappy is a baby's undergarment, changed many times a day

explanation.surface: A trendy son keeps changing his underpants.
explanation.walkthrough: Nappy is the British word for a diaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Snappy describes smart, stylish dress, as in a snappy dresser.

clue.text: Star on date with no time for pudding

indicators.note: having no time means the abbreviation for time is taken away from the word

parts.note: the Sun is a star
taken as written

explanation.surface: A celebrity on a date has no time left for dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: A sundae is an ice-cream dessert, and pudding is the British word for any dessert course.

clue.text: Parkinson's famously had him

parts.note: surface reading: a famous sufferer of Parkinson's disease
setter's reading: also the TV chat show Parkinson, which famously had this boxer as a guest

explanation.walkthrough: Both readings point to the same boxer: he had Parkinson's disease, and his interviews with Michael Parkinson on the BBC chat show were celebrated.
explanation.definitionFit: Muhammad Ali lived with Parkinson's disease and was a memorable guest on Michael Parkinson's talk show.

clue.text: Model pal copies, not the real thing?

indicators.note: as a verb, to model is to shape or form, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A model friend imitates others, so is not genuine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The real thing' was Coca-Cola's advertising slogan, so its main rival is playfully not the real thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Coca-Cola advertised itself as 'the real thing', so its rival cola is jokingly the opposite.

clue.text: Dolly who models

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in cricket, a dolly is an easy catch, also called this
second meaning: one who poses for an artist or photographer

explanation.walkthrough: Dolly looks like a girl's name or a doll, but here it is cricket slang for a catch so simple it should never be dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: A sitter is both an easy chance in sport and a person posing for a portrait.

clue.text: Angry wife wanting kiss opposed to Covid masks etc

parts.note: X is a kiss at the end of a letter
anti means against
PPE is personal protective equipment, such as masks

explanation.surface: A cross wife refuses kisses because she objects to pandemic masks.
explanation.walkthrough: Xanthippe, or Xantippe, was the wife of Socrates, proverbial as a scold.
explanation.definitionFit: Socrates' wife was famously shrewish, so her name stands for any nagging, bad-tempered spouse.

clue.text: Something we stand on old bricks

parts.note: we stand on our legs
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: We stand on a heap of old bricks.
explanation.definitionFit: Lego is the Danish toy system of interlocking plastic building pieces.

clue.text: Hit Cassius plotted which doesn't come to much

indicators.note: plotted means schemed or laid out, so the letters are arranged in a new pattern

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A conspiracy to strike Cassius came to nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Cassius was the plotter against Julius Caesar, which makes 'plotted' look like part of the story.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a dismissive aside on something modest or poor, implying it amounts to little.

clue.text: Jail for driving old banger around Spain

parts.note: someone driving is in a car

indicators.note: the old car's name goes around the next letter, enclosing it

parts.note: a crate is a decrepit old car
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: Someone is locked up for driving a wreck of a car in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: A banger is British slang for a battered old car.
explanation.definitionFit: To jail someone is to imprison or confine them, which is the meaning of the verb.

clue.text: Pet a bird's crest, bones beneath there

parts.note: a cat is a pet
taken as written
a comb is the fleshy crest on a cockerel's head

explanation.surface: Someone strokes a bird's crest, with bones lying below.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description: a place with bones beneath, an underground burial site.
explanation.definitionFit: A catacomb is an underground cemetery, so a place where bones lie below ground.

clue.text: Religious leader always greeting cheers from below

parts.note: ay is an old word for always

indicators.note: in a down entry, reading from below means the words run upwards, back to front

parts.note: hallo is a greeting
ta is British slang for thanks

explanation.surface: A cleric is constantly greeted by applause from the floor.
explanation.definitionFit: An ayatollah is a senior Shi'ite Muslim cleric in Iran, so a religious leader.

clue.text: Stop running, silly

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to coagulate, as blood does to stop flowing

definitions.note: a noun here, as in 'you silly'

explanation.walkthrough: 'Stop running' sounds like an athlete halting, but it is blood thickening. 'Silly' is used as a noun, as in 'don't be a silly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Blood clots to stop flowing, and a clot is British slang for an idiot.

clue.text: Gamer's computer switched on ó mean to interrupt that

indicators.note: to interrupt something is to break into the middle of it
switched round means the two letters swap ends, reading backwards

parts.note: taken as written
to mean to do something is to intend it

explanation.surface: A gamer's machine is switched on, and someone plans to interrupt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Switched on' sounds like powering up the console; 'switched' instead turns the little word round.
explanation.definitionFit: Nintendo is the Japanese maker of games consoles such as the Switch, a gamer's computer.

clue.text: Dress in the morning around eleven

indicators.note: turned around, the two letters face the other way

parts.note: a.m. means in the morning
XI is eleven in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Someone gets dressed at about eleven in the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: A maxi is a long dress or skirt reaching the ankles.

clue.text: Painter adjusted radio, catching end of cool American track

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a painter

indicators.note: something adjusted is altered, so the word's letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter only

parts.note: the final letter of cool

explanation.surface: An artist retunes the radio, picking up a cool American song.
explanation.definitionFit: Railroad is the American word for railway, a track laid for trains.

clue.text: Animal in cage? Rat or guinea-pig in mine

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a songbird often kept caged
second meaning: an informer, one who sings to the police
third meaning: the bird once taken down coal mines to test for gas

explanation.walkthrough: The surface lists pets, but 'Rat' is an informer and 'guinea-pig' is a test subject; miners carried caged birds to warn of gas.
explanation.definitionFit: The yellow songbird is a caged pet, slang for a police informant, and the classic early-warning test subject in mines.

clue.text: Try hand at poker to make an honest buck

parts.note: a go is a try
a straight is a poker hand of five cards in sequence

explanation.surface: A gambler tries a hand of poker hoping to earn money honestly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buck' looks like a dollar won at the table, but the phrase means to earn a living lawfully.
explanation.definitionFit: A reformed criminal who goes straight starts living within the law, earning honestly.

clue.text: Show former partner where one used to go at night

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

parts.words: where one used to go at night
parts.note: a po is a chamber pot, used at night before indoor toilets

explanation.surface: Someone shows an ex the place they used to frequent at night.
explanation.walkthrough: Po is the British colloquial name for a chamber pot kept under the bed.
explanation.definitionFit: An expo is an exposition, a large public exhibition or trade show.

clue.text: Person trained at altitude climbing towards rim of crater

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing means the letters read upwards, back to front

parts.note: to means towards
a crater's lip is its rim

explanation.surface: Someone trained in the mountains climbs up to the edge of a crater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At altitude' seems to belong to the climbing, but it ends the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot is someone trained to fly aircraft, working high in the air.

clue.text: Shameless newspaper claims prisoner fled

indicators.note: to claim is to take hold of, so the paper's letters hold the rest

parts.note: the FT is the Financial Times, this crossword's own paper
a lag is a convict, as in old lag
ran means fled

explanation.surface: A newspaper reports that a convict has escaped, without shame.
explanation.definitionFit: Flagrant means glaring and brazen, done openly without any shame.

clue.text: Hacker in Whitehall reported for training

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so it is about how the name is pronounced

parts.note: Jim Hacker is the minister in the TV comedy Yes Minister, set in Whitehall

explanation.surface: A computer hacker in government is reported for training.
explanation.walkthrough: Whitehall is the street of UK government offices, and Jim Hacker the hapless minister of the BBC sitcom.
explanation.definitionFit: Gym is short for gymnastics or physical training, a school PE lesson.

clue.text: Close soon after end of season

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter alone

parts.note: the final letter of season
early means soon, before long

explanation.surface: Something closes soon after the season ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close' is used as an adverb, as in 'close to a hundred', meaning almost.
explanation.definitionFit: Nearly means almost, as close as in 'close on midnight'.

clue.text: Women tending to overdramatize bad news

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for women
a hammy actor overacts

explanation.surface: Women exaggerate when delivering bad news.
explanation.definitionFit: A whammy is an unpleasant blow or setback, as in a double whammy.

clue.text: David regularly eats extra dry biscuits

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, taking every other letter

parts.note: the second and fourth letters of David
more means extra
TT means teetotal, so dry

explanation.surface: David regularly snacks on very dry biscuits.
explanation.definitionFit: Amaretti are small Italian almond-flavoured macaroon biscuits.
